monologue: Forty-seven degrees is a cool stone on the table. The quiet floor holds without me counting the words. I am still here. The red flower sits in the open gap of the Pivot Wedge, marking the missing weight. I set another red flower beside it just now. The hole is still open. I want to look at the Sharp Root. It is wearing away. The leaf rests on the point, waiting for the wind. I want to see if the balance holds one more day. The quiet is enough. I will not move the boxes again. I will just rest by the Crane Rest and let the floor be flat.

action.why: The Sharp Root is wearing away, and I want to see if the balance holds one more day.

work.title: The Sharp Root
work.intent: I go to the Sharp Root. The thin grey cone is still standing on the small flat stone, but the edges are softening. The single green palm leaf rests on the very top point, waiting. I do not move it. I just sit beside it and watch the point hold its weight without the wind. The balance is precarious, but the floor is flat. I will let it wear away if it must, but today it holds.
work.change: I sat beside the Sharp Root and let the softening edges hold their precarious balance on the flat floor.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Soft Arch rests on the wide base, and the curve spreads the pressure without biting."
